subject: GCP private offer: tiered crediting and reseller mapping
content:
From: Sam Choi <sam.choi@acme-tech.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@cloudbridge.com, po-ops@marketplace.gcp.example
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: GCP private offer — crediting approach + reseller pass-through

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move to a private offer on GCP but have two asks before we sign: 1) a clear tiered credit schedule for list-price overages vs committed usage, and 2) how credits/discounts flow to our reseller (CloudBridge) — they need to see pass-through amounts documented for their procurement.

Can you send a sample credit table and tell us what split options Redwood supports for reseller netbacks (e.g., gross pass-through vs. list-price holdback)? We'll need this for our internal procurement and legal.

Thanks,
Sam Choi
Head of Cloud Procurement
Acme Tech

---
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Sam Choi <sam.choi@acme-tech.com>
Cc: partners@cloudbridge.com, po-ops@marketplace.gcp.example
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — crediting approach + reseller pass-through

Sam —

Appreciate the clear asks. I attached an initial draft of a tiered credit schedule (proposed_credit_schedule.xlsx) and a reseller mapping CSV for CloudBridge (reseller_mapping_v2.csv). High level:

- We can do both committed-anchored credits (monthly true-up style) and list-price overage credits.
- Typical pass-through options:
  * 100% gross pass-through to reseller (no holdback)
  * 85/15 split (reseller/netback) where Redwood retains small holdback to cover marketplace fees
  * Hybrid: gross pass-through for committed buckets, holdback on overages

Before I lock this down in the private offer, I want to validate the preferred split with our channel team and confirm any Marketplace Ops constraints. Looping in Ben and Karthik internally; Ben for channel economics and Karthik for marketplace packaging (SKU buckets & commit phasing).

Are there any regulatory or billing constraints on your side we should know about?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0167

---
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: GCP private offer — crediting approach + reseller pass-through

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Sam's note and the attachments. Quick asks from Acme: a tiered credit schedule they can present to procurement, and explicit guidance on how credits will be shown to CloudBridge on their invoices (they asked for a documented pass-through percentage).

Notes from the account: Acme expects a 12–18 month commit with 3-4 tiered volume bands. They want clarity on overage credits versus committed credits (i.e., do we net overages against the commit or treat separately with a different unit credit?). They also prefer minimal friction for the reseller — ideally 100% pass-through, but procurement expects Redwood to hold back something to cover marketplace fees.

Can we propose a conservative default that balances unit economics and partner friendliness?

Jasmine

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: GCP private offer — crediting approach + reseller pass-through

Jasmine —

Quick take: propose default 90% gross pass-through, 10% Redwood holdback for marketplace and deferred rebates. Rationale: keeps the reseller mostly whole for procurement checks, preserves us a margin buffer (marketplace fees + small ops reserve). For committed buckets we can offer a slightly better split (93/7) because gross LTV is guaranteed.

On the crediting table: recommend explicit rows for:
- Committed discount bucket (monthly committed consumption) — credit applies as an upfront effective unit price across the commit band.
- Overage pricing — distinct per-token or per-unit credit that applies at true-up; suggest a conservative overage credit of 40% off list for first tier, 25% for second tier.
- Retro credits for missed performance (rare) — negotiated case-by-case.

I'll draft a short blurb we can include in the private offer terms explaining the invoice line items: gross list, partner pass-through, Redwood holdback, marketplace fee. Karthik — does GCP marketplace allow explicit partner-pass-through lines in the invoice metadata?

Ben
Head of Channel Partnerships | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: GCP private offer — crediting approach + reseller pass-through

Ben / Jasmine —

Confirming: GCP supports custom private offers with line-item metadata but has limitations around automated partner invoice passthrough. Marketplace Ops will need the reseller mapping CSV (I reviewed the attached) to ensure the partner_id is present on the PO. Two practical constraints:
1) Invoice display: we can include partner pass-through as a separate invoice line if CloudBridge is onboarded as a marketplace partner with partner_id attached to the private offer. If not, the fallback is to annotate the private offer terms and provide a reconciled spreadsheet for Acme and CloudBridge monthly.
2) Credits at true-up: GCP allows retroactive crediting but the timing can be monthly or quarterly depending on billing cycles. Recommend monthly true-up to keep cashflow predictable for Acme.

I'll update the proposed_credit_schedule.xlsx to reflect the monthly true-up cadence and add a short Marketplace Ops preface. Also, Ben — tagging you to confirm the suggested splits (90/10, 93/7 for committed).

Karthik
Senior Marketplace Program Manager | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

---
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Sam Choi <sam.choi@acme-tech.com>
Cc: partners@cloudbridge.com, po-ops@marketplace.gcp.example, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — crediting approach + reseller pass-through

Sam —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are the updated files: proposed_credit_schedule.xlsx (monthly true-up cadence, three committed bands with per-unit effective pricing and separate overage credit rows) and reseller_mapping_v2.csv (includes CloudBridge partner_id placeholder). Summary of the proposal:

- Crediting model:
  * Commit bands (12–18 month): Tier 1 (0–$250k) effective unit X with 12% committed credit, Tier 2 ($250k–$750k) 18% committed credit, Tier 3 ($750k+) 22% committed credit.
  * Overages: First overage tier: 40% off list, second overage tier: 25% off list. Overage credits apply during monthly true-up.
  * Retro adjustments handled monthly; Redwood provides a reconciliation CSV with invoice metadata for Acme and CloudBridge.

- Reseller pass-through: default suggested split 90% pass-through to CloudBridge / 10% Redwood holdback. For committed buckets we can offer 93% pass-through / 7% holdback if Acme signs a firm 18-month commit. If CloudBridge requires explicit invoice line items, Karthik's team will need CloudBridge's partner_id to be attached to the private offer in Marketplace Ops.

Next steps:
1) Sam — confirm whether Acme prefers 12 vs 18 month commit and whether they want 100% pass-through (we can quote but will require marketplace fee coverage in the offer).
2) CloudBridge — please confirm partner_id or advise if you prefer a reconciled monthly spreadsheet instead of line-item pass-through.
3) If we have agreement, I'll open the private offer draft and attach the credit table as exhibit A.

If helpful I can also set a 30-minute call to walk procurement + CloudBridge through the table.

Best regards,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0167

Attachments: proposed_credit_schedule.xlsx (updated), reseller_mapping_v2.csv
